claims.text: The starting material is a bulk, as-cast, chemically disordered, equimolar Ta–Nb–Hf–Zr–Ti high-entropy alloy.
Applying high hydrostatic pressure compresses the Ta–Nb–Hf–Zr–Ti alloy.
Pressure-induced compression modifies the alloy's lattice parameters.
Pressure-induced compression modifies the alloy's electronic band structure.
Pressure changes electron density and local bonding environments in the alloy.
Lattice compression reduces interatomic distances and enhances orbital overlap.
Pressure modifies the alloy's vibrational phonon modes.
The pressure-induced electronic and phonon changes increase electron–phonon coupling.
Increased electron–phonon coupling promotes Cooper-pair formation and triggers or enhances superconductivity.
Increasing pressure should produce a systematic emergence of superconductivity or an increase in superconducting transition temperature.
At ambient pressure, the alloy is expected either not to superconduct or to have a substantially lower transition temperature than under high pressure.
The proposed pressure effect should hold up to approximately 100 GPa if the crystal structure remains unchanged.
A pressure-induced structural phase transition marks the boundary beyond which the proposed mechanism is not claimed to hold.
The controlled test varies pressure from ambient to approximately 100 GPa while holding sample preparation and cooling rate constant.
Superconductivity will be assessed below 10 K using resistivity, magnetic susceptibility, and critical-current measurements.
In-situ high-pressure X-ray diffraction will be used to determine whether a structural phase transition occurs.
Sample-homogeneity variations may influence the observed pressure dependence.

contradictions.description: The boundary excludes pressure-induced structural phase transitions from the hypothesis's domain, whereas the falsification rule treats a phase transition correlated with superconductivity as falsifying the hypothesis. An observation outside the stated validity domain should not itself falsify the within-domain claim.
